lesson_aotfw_008/block_l008_002/student: An Artist of the Floating World

As you read, note moments where Ono contradicts his earlier account of the same event. These revisions are not errors—they are the novel's central evidence that identity is constructed through narrative.
In this lesson we consolidate our reading of

by examining how Masuji Ono's memories of the floating world, his wartime propaganda, and his role as a father combine to form an identity that is continually rewritten. Ishiguro does not present memory as a neutral archive; instead, recollection becomes a form of self-defence.
